notes.1a: Many candidates correctly stated that the hazard of one of the solutions was corrosive and the level of risk was medium or high.
notes.1i: Some candidates correctly stated that two variables which needed to be standardised were the volume of urine, the volumes of K and C and the amount of shaking of the solutions when mixing. The better performing candidates then described the use of syringes to deliver the necessary volumes or an appropriate method for standardising the mixing of the solutions.
notes.1ii: The majority of candidates drew the graph, using the headings given in the table, with protein concentration / µg cm –3 on the x-axis and absorbance on the y-axis. The better performing candidates used scales of 200 to 2 cm, labelled at least each 2 cm for the x-axis and 0.2 to 2 cm, labelled at least each 2 cm for the y-axis, plotted the points exactly with a small cross or dot in a circle and drew a sharp, clear ruled line accurately connecting each of the points or using a line of best fit.
notes.1iii: Most candidates drew a circle on the graph to show that the anomalous result was the plot at 200 µm cm –3 (protein concentration) / 0.36 (absorbance).
notes.1iv: Many candidates correctly estimated the concentration of protein with an absorbance of 0.49 according to their results. The better performing candidates stated the units as µg cm –3 .
notes.1v: Most candidates correctly identified one significant source of error as the difficulty of judging the colour of the solution.
notes.2i: Many candidates correctly measured the diameter of the cells labelled D, E, F, G and H to the correct degree of accuracy, showed the conversion from millimetres to micrometres (multiplying by 1000) and showed division by the magnification (1430). The better performing candidates showed their working.
notes.2ii: Many candidates showed the addition of the measurements from (c)(i), showed the division by 5 and included the correct units (µm).
notes.2iii: Some candidates were able to suggest that the reason for the observed difference between cells D and Z was due to the different water potentials between the cells and the external solutions.
notes.key_messages: (cid:127) When describing graphical results, numerical values extracted should be accompanied by both the x-axis and y-axis descriptions, with units given. (cid:127) A description of a mode of transmission for a named disease must show understanding that the pathogen is passed from an infected person to an uninfected person. (cid:127) The shape of the active site of an enzyme, when compared to its specific substrate shape, should be described as complementary, and not as similar, same or matching.
